title: Make a Positive Array
statement:
Call an array **positive** when every subarray (a contiguous run of elements) with at least three elements has a sum strictly greater than `0`; subarrays of length 1 or 2 are not checked.

In one operation you may pick any element of `nums` and overwrite it with any integer from `-10^18` to `10^18`. Return the minimum number of operations that makes `nums` positive.
notes:
## Intuition

A replaced element can be given a value like `10^18`, which outweighs everything else, so every subarray that contains it becomes positive, while subarrays that avoid it keep their old sums. The task is therefore to pick as few positions as possible so that every **bad** subarray (at least 3 elements, sum `<= 0`) contains one of them. Trying every set of positions works but is exponential. Instead sweep left to right: when the first bad subarray ends at `end`, one of its elements must be replaced, and the last one, `nums[end]`, also covers the most subarrays further right. Everything through `end` is then safe, so the search restarts just after it.

## Approach

1. Build `prefix`, where `prefix[i]` is the sum of the first `i` numbers, so `nums[start..end]` sums to `prefix[end + 1] - prefix[start]`.
2. Move `end` from 2 to `n - 1`. The newest start that leaves at least 3 elements is `start = end - 2`; if it lies after `lastReplaced`, fold `prefix[start]` into `maxPrefix`.
3. Some allowed subarray ending at `end` is bad exactly when `prefix[end + 1] <= maxPrefix`.
4. Then replace `nums[end]`: add one to `operations`, set `lastReplaced = end` and reset `maxPrefix`, because later subarrays must start after `end`.
5. Return `operations`.

## Example 1, step by step

`prefix = [0, -10, 5, -7]`. At `end = 2`, `start = 0` is allowed, so `maxPrefix = prefix[0] = 0`. Since `prefix[3] = -7 <= 0`, the whole array is bad: replace `nums[2]` and set `operations = 1`. No ends remain, so the answer is `1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass builds `prefix` and one pass sweeps `end`.
- Space: O(n) for `prefix`.

## Pitfalls

- A sum of exactly 0 is not positive: `[0, 0, 0]` needs one operation.
- Checking only triples is not enough: in `[-5, 3, 3, -5]` both triples sum to 1, but the whole array sums to -4.
- After a replacement, ignore starts at or before `lastReplaced`; those subarrays contain the huge value.
- Sums reach about 10^14, so Java and C need 64-bit integers for `prefix`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `prefix` | `prefix[i]` is the sum of the first `i` numbers |
| `operations` | replacements made so far |
| `lastReplaced` | index of the latest replaced element (-1 before any) |
| `maxPrefix` | the largest `prefix[start]` over the allowed starts so far |
| `end` | last index of the subarrays being checked |
| `start` | the newest allowed first index, `end - 2` |
